messages:
Priya Nair: Quick check — POC customer (EU fintech) wants strict geo-gating: all inference and logs must stay in EU. They also need IP ranges to allowlist and the current sub-processor inventory for their security team. Can we provide these for the POC?
Tom Kendrick: Are they planning to use Hosted or Dedicated for the POC? Hosted has regional endpoints; Dedicated gives more isolation and control (and usually static egress options).
Priya Nair: They want hosted first to move fast but will consider Dedicated if we can’t guarantee IPs/eSNI. For POC they asked for: 1) subproc list, 2) egress IPs/CIDRs (staging), 3) routing policy example to pin to eu.
Alex Garcia: We can provide current subprocessor inventory link and a short attestation. Note hosted traffic may egress through cloud provider infra (GCP/AWS) + CDN/proxy subprocessors. Subproc doc: https://redwood.internal/subprocs/current (internal link)
Priya Nair: Customer security team insists on CIDRs (not hostnames). Can we give a set for staging? They want to put in their firewall rules.
Alex Garcia: For hosted we don't publish stable global static CIDRs per customer. We can provide a recommended staging allowlist (region-scoped) but it's not SLA-backed. If they need static egress IPs we should propose Dedicated paired with their VPC or Redwood Private. Example: Dedicated + customer NAT -> stable egress.
Marta Varela: From legal: we can share the current subprocessor inventory and our standard data residency controls, but we cannot contractually guarantee a static provider list will never change. For POC we can provide a signed attestation snapshot.
Priya Nair: Also the customer asked about failover: they want failover inside EU only. If eu-west runs out of capacity they want eu-central, not APAC or US. Can routing do that?
Alex Garcia: Yes — routing policies support region pinning + controlled fallback list. You can configure strict pinning (deny fallback) or an ordered EU-only fallback. Note cache/KV prefixes: if you enable global KV cache it might replicate; ensure cache residency is disabled for strict EU. Example config we can share:
```
routing_policy:
  primary_region: "eu-west-1"
  fallback_regions: ["eu-central-1"]
  allow_fallback: false
  cache_residency: "region-isolated"
```
Tom Kendrick: On pricing: adding dedicated isolation / per-region pinning for POC typically has a small uplift (mostly operational overhead). For a short POC we usually add a one-time POC ops fee + 10-20% on top of hosted per-token estimate to cover reserved capacity. I can get a ballpark number if you want.
Eli Chen: Yes please. Customer will need an estimate for budgeting. Also we should send the security questionnaire answers and the attestation. Can someone assemble a one-pager (subproc list + allowlist CIDRs for staging + routing snippet + pricing note) by EOD?
Alex Garcia: I can draft the network piece (CIDRs for EU staging + routing snippet). Will mark them as non-SLA and label for POC only.
Marta Varela: I'll prepare the attestation and answer the top security questionnaire items (subproc, data flow, encryption). Will add a note about change notifications and PRR process.
Priya Nair: Great — can we schedule a quick 30m with customer's infra + security tomorrow? Timezone CET.
Eli Chen: I'll propose 10:30 CET tomorrow and include a pre-read with the one-pager.
OpsBot: Notice — cert rotation for eu-west-1 scheduled in 6 days (no expected impact).
Priya Nair: Thanks all — leaving this thread here. If anyone changes scope pls ping me. :thumbsup:
